items.claim: A target element that leaves the document leaves the loop stuck (A+B, B's swapped-target case)
`watchElementMove` frames an unclipped element against the top-level viewport inside an iframe
An injected `requestFrame` with no `cancelFrame` cancels unrelated window frames
items.note: The canceller is now captured with the clock that scheduled the frame. A loop on its own clock with no `cancelFrame` cancels nothing, and leaves stale frames to the existing stale-callback check.

items.claim: leakProbe keeps a timer cleared by the other kind's clear function
leakProbe records a listener added with an already-aborted signal
actSettled's release removes a frame stub installed inside it
A clock that calls back synchronously leaves the loop holding a dead handle
`useNearViewport` never observes an element mounted later or swapped in
leakProbe misses a `once` listener's removal when the listener stops propagation
B's "cancel with a non-default clock" finding
leakProbe never counted listeners added on `window`. vitest's jsdom environment puts a bound `addEventListener` on the global scope, which skips the prototype patch
leakProbe threw a TypeError for any element listener given a `signal`, because vitest's `AbortSignal` comes from another realm
